comparison: Both evaluations SUPPORT claims C13-C18 regarding DNA extraction and ddPCR quantification. OpenEval notes strong experimental evidence with quantitative data and near-perfect linear regression. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly confirms 'clear evidence for the value of the direct buffer extraction system' and 'utility of ddPCR for quantification.' Full agreement on these methodological claims.

DISAGREEMENT on evaluation type for claims C19-C23, C27-C29. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with well-supported experimental data. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 raising critical concerns that 'detection of bacterial genomes does not equate to viable bacterial cells' and questioning whether extracellular DNA from lysed cells contributes to ddPCR results. Peer review also addresses C30 and C32 (phenotypic variations), which OpenEval evaluates separately in R4.

Both evaluations SUPPORT claims C24-C26 regarding dose-dependent effects on host cell viability. OpenEval notes clear demonstration with statistical analysis but mentions missing details on replicates and normalization. Peer Reviewer 3 describes the phenomenology as 'interesting and well-described' without questioning the host cell genome data specifically. Strong agreement.

Both address phenotypic variation claims C30 and C32. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with reasonable mechanistic interpretation, though noting direct SCV characterization would strengthen conclusions. Peer review includes these claims in their UNCERTAIN evaluation (R2), with concerns about whether genome counts reflect viable bacteria versus dead cell DNA, which affects interpretation of the discrepancy.

Both evaluations SUPPORT claims C33-C39 regarding clinical diagnostic evidence. OpenEval notes strong support from clinical, histological, and microbiological evidence despite limited sample size (n=3). Peer reviewers acknowledge 'compelling' results with 'real-world clinical implications' and note the limited sample size does not undermine acceptance of findings. Strong agreement.

Both evaluations SUPPORT claims C40-C43 regarding sequencing data and bacterial detection in culture-negative samples. OpenEval notes well-supported data with appropriate controls but mentions missing information on read mapping. Peer Reviewer 2 confirms authors 'demonstrate PCR evidence that S. aureus can be detected' in clinical samples. Agreement on the validity of detection methods.

Both evaluations SUPPORT claims C44-C48 regarding tuf gene selection and methodology. OpenEval notes well-justified choice with reasonable inferences, though experimental validation comparing tuf vs. 16S would strengthen claims. Peer Reviewer 3 finds 'the successful application of MinION technology to sequence the EF-Tu amplicons from clinical samples is of interest' and implicitly accepts the methodological choice. Strong agreement.

Both evaluations SUPPORT claims C52-C54 regarding workflow advantages. OpenEval notes demonstrated advantages but lacks direct time/cost comparisons for 'rapid and labor-saving' claims. Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly states 'clear evidence for the value of the direct buffer extraction system' and 'utility of ddPCR for quantification.' Agreement on methodological value.

Both evaluations rate as UNCERTAIN claims C49-C51, C55-C56 regarding clinical utility and future applications. OpenEval notes these are speculative 'potential' applications without actual clinical validation or demonstrated timelines. Peer Reviewer 3 questions 'the significance of these results outside the model osteocyte system' and states 'it is hard to see how enumeration could have value beyond in vitro and animal model studies.' Strong agreement on uncertainty about clinical translation.

OpenEval evaluates claim C57 (recommendation to use both CFU and ddPCR methods) as SUPPORTED, noting it represents sound scientific practice. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific recommendation.

OpenEval evaluates claims C1-C2, C4-C5 (established knowledge about culture-negative osteomyelitis) as SUPPORTED background information. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluates claims C6-C9, C58-C62 (established knowledge and model system descriptions) as SUPPORTED methodological details and background. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these descriptive claims.

OpenEval evaluates claim C3 (central finding about ddPCR quantification discrepancies) as SUPPORTED by extensive experimental data. No separate peer review evaluation found specifically for this summary claim, though related evidence is discussed in peer R2 and R4.
